sources.entry: Eclipse - Eclipse is an open-source integrated development environment (IDE) used in computer programming, featuring a base workspace and an extensible plug-in system for customizing the environment.

summary.one_liner: Eclipse Platform repository holding the core Java modules (resources, runtime, debug, team, terminal, and others) that form the basis of the Eclipse IDE.
summary.what_it_does: This repository is the platform layer beneath the Eclipse IDE, organized into several modules. The resources module provides workspace, folder, file, and file-system abstractions with interfaces like IResource. The runtime module provides IJob and ISchedulingRule and schedules multithreaded jobs with exclusive resource access. The debug module offers a language-agnostic framework with interfaces such as ILaunchConfiguration, IDebugTarget, and IBreakpoint. The team module supplies interfaces for version control integration, resource synchronization, and two- and three-way comparison and merging. The terminal module provides an embeddable terminal widget supporting local, SSH, and Telnet connections, and the update module covers runtime platform configuration. The platform module supplies images such as the splash screen.
use_cases: Building plug-ins for the Eclipse IDE
Understanding Eclipse workspace and resource APIs
Creating background jobs with resource locking in Java
Integrating version control into an Eclipse-based tool
Embedding a terminal widget with SSH or Telnet in a Java app
Building a language-agnostic debugger front end
notable: Contains the core modules that make up the Eclipse IDE foundation
Provides a reusable embeddable terminal widget with local, SSH, and Telnet support
Language-agnostic debug framework with launch configuration and breakpoint interfaces
Job scheduling with exclusive access to resources
caveats: The README gives no build or run instructions, so this is a source repository for the platform rather than a standalone app
Developed mainly by volunteers, so not every reported issue may be addressed
